// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// In-memory stand-ins for globals the Worker reaches for. Node gives us
// Request/Response/fetch/URL natively; we only need to fake `caches.default`
// and route outbound `fetch` calls. The tests call the default export's
// fetch handler directly — no wrangler, no miniflare, no real network.
// ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

interface CacheEntry {
  body: ArrayBuffer;
  headers: [string, string][];
}

function createCache() {
  const store = new Map<string, CacheEntry>();
  const cache = {
    async match(req: Request | string): Promise<Response | undefined> {
      const url = typeof req === "string" ? req : req.url;
      const entry = store.get(url);
      if (!entry) return undefined;
      return new Response(entry.body.slice(0), { headers: entry.headers });
    },
    async put(req: Request | string, res: Response): Promise<void> {
      const url = typeof req === "string" ? req : req.url;
      const body = await res.arrayBuffer();
      const headers: [string, string][] = [];
      res.headers.forEach((value, key) => headers.push([key, value]));
      store.set(url, { body, headers });
    },
    async delete(req: Request | string): Promise<boolean> {
      const url = typeof req === "string" ? req : req.url;
      return store.delete(url);
    },
    // helpers for assertions
    _keys: () => Array.from(store.keys()),
    _size: () => store.size,
  };
  return cache;
}

---
type: note
status: inbox
created: 2026-04-11
---

# Preserve original APOD filename on download

When a user downloads an image from `api.nasapicture.com` (or `get.`), the browser saves it as `api.nasapicture.jpg`, derived from the hostname because the URL path has no meaningful filename. We should set `Content-Disposition` so downloads use the original NASA asset name (e.g. `NGC1234_hubble1200.jpg`), preserving provenance and making the filename searchable against apod.nasa.gov.

## Problem

All image endpoints currently return only `Content-Type`, so browsers fall back to `<hostname>.<ext>` when the user hits "Save image as...". Every image from the proxy ends up named the same thing, which is unhelpful for anyone collecting wallpapers or citing sources.

## Proposed fix

Add a `Content-Disposition: inline; filename="<original>"` header to image responses. Using `inline` (not `attachment`) keeps the image displayed in-browser when hit directly, and only influences the filename on save.

The original filename is always the last path segment of the NASA URL:


==> board/planning/NOTE-0028_claude-md-scripts-drift-check.md <==
---
type: note
status: inbox
created: 2026-04-11
---

# Drift check between CLAUDE.md commands and package.json scripts

The Commands section in `CLAUDE.md` hand-lists every npm script with a short description. It's useful curation (I can tell Claude *why* a command matters), but it silently drifts as scripts are added, renamed, or removed. Package.json can't natively import scripts from another file, so keeping them in sync needs tooling.

## Options considered

1. **`@package.json` reference in CLAUDE.md** — auto-syncs but pulls in deps/config noise and drops the inline annotations.
2. **Generator script** — maintain a `scripts.json` source of truth; a node script writes both `package.json` scripts and a marker-delimited block in CLAUDE.md on `prepare` or pre-commit. Most machinery, strongest guarantee.
3. **Drift check test** (this note) — a small vitest that parses `package.json` and asserts every script is mentioned in `CLAUDE.md` (or vice versa). Doesn't own the content, just catches staleness.

## Proposed approach

A single vitest under `test/` that:
